desc:
Over the last six months, frontend frameworks written in Rust and WebAssembly have begun overturning the old narrative that WASM is too slow for DOM rendering. In this video we'll take a look at several Rust/WASM frameworks to try to understand the truth about Rust/WASM performance.

EDIT: To clarify about the memory usage: Something changed in the benchmark at some point in the way memory use is

recs.x:
WASM has no native access to the DOM, so all DOM manipulations from wasm-land have to go through JS bindings with all the (de)serialisation costs that go with crossing the language boundary. That eats up a lot of whatever performance gains you'd see from rust-on-wasm for pure compute.
